newsitem.title: FINLAND: NOKIA JUMPS AS MOTOROLA Q4 ENCOURAGES.
newsitem.headline: NOKIA JUMPS AS MOTOROLA Q4 ENCOURAGES.

text.p: Shares in Finnish telecoms group Nokia Oy rose sharply on Friday after its U.S. rival Motorola reported encouraging Q4 earnings late on Thursday.
At 1100/0900 GMT, Nokia stood at 301.00 markka, up 8.50 markka or almost three percent in brisk trade.
Analysts said Motorola's results showed improvement in mobile phones and that this was likely to be a result of U.S. market growth rather than increased market share.
"Our basic view has not changed, but if (Nokia profit) forecasts for 1997 and 1998 are revised, they will be raised," said Jaakko Niemela, chief analyst at brokerage Opstock.
Motorola's fourth quarter earnings were slightly short of expectations -- $0.39 per share versus an average forecast of $0.41 -- but its comments sparked hopes, Finnish analysts said.

The big question now was how much of Motorola's growth in mobile phones had been due to higher market share and how much had stemmed from U.S. market expansion, which would also be good for Nokia and Swedish Ericsson , they said.
"The key question is whether Motorola's bottoming out reflects a pick-up on the U.S. market or whether Motorola is recouping lost market share," said one.
